$comment: The newest supported release of every runtime, OS and base image the repository chooses, and the oldest release each pin may name (#715, #714).
scripts/version-floors.test.mjs reads every pin in the tree and fails any below its floor, naming the file, the pin and the floor.
.github/workflows/update-version-floors.yml re-reads the sources below every week and opens one pull request when a floor moves; that pull request's CI then shows which pins are behind.
Python's floor lives here rather than in a separate scripts/python-floor.json, which #714 first proposed: one file, one rule per kind.
checkedOn is the day an entry last moved against its source, not the day it was last read: the weekly job writes nothing in a week when nothing moved, the same convention as AVM_VERIFIED_ON.

python.rule: The newest release line, no more than two patch releases behind that line's newest (N-2 patches). A new line is adopted once its N-2 patch exists (3.15.2 for 3.15). A pin that names the line only (actions/setup-python '3.14') resolves to the newest patch when it runs. Owner rule 2026-09-26 (#714).

node.rule: The newest line the platform that runs it allows, among lines that are or will become LTS; within a line, no more than two minor releases behind that line's newest (N-2 minors), and a new line is adopted once its N-2 minor exists. A component whose platform caps the line is held exactly at that ceiling. A pin that names the line only (actions/setup-node '26') resolves to the newest release when it runs; an engines.node range's lowest admitted version must meet the floor and the range must admit the newest release. Owner direction 2026-09-25: the latest current release line.

functions.rule: Flex Consumption supports Node.js 22 and 24 (both GA) and does not offer 26, so functions/ runs the newest of those two, 24, and every pin that builds, tests, deploys or runs its code names 24 (update-learn-catalogue.yml imports functions/src and resolves functions/node_modules).
appliesTo: .github/workflows/coverage.yml > coverage > Set up Node.js 24 for functions

ubuntu.rule: The newest LTS release only; interim releases get nine months of support and are never used. A host's target (the newest release it accepts) must be the newest LTS; an older LTS it still accepts as a fallback is compatibility, not a target, and is not checked. A workflow's runs-on is held by platformCeilings.runners instead, because GitHub-hosted runners reach a new LTS months after Canonical releases it.

runners.rule: Every runs-on in .github/workflows names exactly this release, as ubuntu-MAJOR.MINOR (ubuntu-26.04), and never ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-slim or any other label without a release. ubuntu-latest is GitHub's pointer, not a release: GitHub moves it on its own schedule, and moves it from 24.04 to 26.04 over 2026-10-19 to 2026-11-19, so for that month the same job can land on either image (https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/14748). newest is the newest x64 ubuntu-MAJOR.04 label the runner-images README lists without a preview or beta badge, and floor equals it. That can sit below the Ubuntu floor for months: Canonical released 26.04 on 2026-04-23, GitHub previewed it on 2026-06-11 and made it generally available on 2026-09-17. It governs every runs-on, so it has no appliesTo list. Owner rule 2026-09-26: the newest LTS OS.

debian.rule: The newest stable major, for a debian image or the Debian release under an official runtime image (python:3.14-slim-trixie).

alpine.rule: Alpine Linux's newest release line, no more than two patch releases behind that line's newest (N-2 patches), the same rule as Python and Terraform; a new line is adopted once its N-2 patch exists (3.25.2 for 3.25). An image pinned by digest must name the exact release its digest is, MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, because a digest does not float: alpine:3.24@sha256:... would meet the floor at line precision whatever patch it holds. The pins are the lab job images in vps-agent/lib/capabilities.js (IMAGES) and any FROM alpine in a tracked Dockerfile. shell-echo ran alpine:3.20, past its end of life on 2026-04-01, until 2026-09-28, with nothing reading that map. Owner rule 2026-09-26 (#714): every runtime, OS and base image on its newest supported release.

terraform.rule: The newest minor line, no more than two patch releases behind its newest (N-2 patches), for an exact pin; a new line is adopted once its N-2 patch exists. Every required_version constraint must admit the newest release.

postgresql.rule: The newest major, no more than two minor releases behind that major's newest (N-2 minors; PostgreSQL numbers its releases MAJOR.MINOR, so 18.6 is minor release 6 of major 18). A new major is adopted once its N-2 minor exists (19.2 for 19). General releases only: the source lists a major from its general release, and the updater also skips any latest release that is not MAJOR.MINOR, so a beta or release candidate (19beta4 was on Docker Hub on 2026-09-26) is never proposed. The pin is coder_postgres_image_tag in lab-host/ansible/group_vars/all.yml, the release Coder's database digest was read from; a major-only tag (18) moves and is refused. https://www.postgresql.org/versions.json agreed on 2026-09-26 (18 current, latestMinor 6). Owner instruction 2026-09-26: the newest general release of PostgreSQL.

vault.rule: HashiCorp Vault's newest release line, no more than two patch releases behind that line's newest (N-2 patches). A new line is adopted the day it is released, with no wait for its N-2 patch: HashiCorp ends the previous community line then (endoflife.date dates the end of life of 2.0 and 1.21 to 2026-08-31 and 2026-04-13, the dates it gives for the releases of 2.1 and 2.0), so waiting would hold the pin on an unsupported line. A line whose latest release is not MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH is skipped. The pin is vault_version in lab-host/ansible/group_vars/all.yml, which must be exactly MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH because the vault role builds the download and SHA256SUMS names from it. api.releases.hashicorp.com agreed on 2026-09-26 (2.1.1, 2026-09-16, the newest community release). Owner decision 2026-09-26: Vault on the lab host.

unsourced.$comment: Things the repository pins that no endoflife.date product covers. Each says so rather than borrowing another source: every floor under kinds comes from endoflife.date's v1 API, which is what the weekly workflow reads, except that a platform ceiling reads what its platform offers from the platform's own page (Microsoft Learn for Flex Consumption, the actions/runner-images README for GitHub-hosted runners). Nothing here is judged or moved by a script; each pin moves by hand.

portainer.rule: The newest LTS release of Portainer Business Edition. Portainer publishes LTS and STS lines; an STS line is superseded within weeks and gets no patch releases after that, so the pin follows LTS. Owner decision 2026-09-26: Portainer on the lab host.
portainer.why: endoflife.date has no Portainer product: https://endoflife.date/api/v1/products/portainer/ answered HTTP 404 on 2026-09-26. Releases are read by hand from https://github.com/portainer/portainer/releases, whose release titles say LTS or STS (2.45.1 LTS, 2026-09-17, was the newest on 2026-09-26); lab-host/ansible/roles/portainer/README.md, "Bumping the pin", has the lines.
